1.content: Build a native app with MoonBit components and fast incremental builds. QuickGUI for MoonBit uses child lists, fluent properties, and fine-grained signals. Components create retained native nodes; changes update only their bindings. Go is also available in the sidebar picker.
1.keywords: moonbit install moon build counter quick git 安装 构建 インストール ビルド

2.content: MoonBit toolchain (tested with moon 0.1.20260827 / moonc v0.10.11 ) Bun 1.3 or newer A C compiler; on macOS, install Xcode Command Line Tools Build on the OS and architecture you are targeting. macOS has native runtime validation; Linux and Windows still need runtime and visual acceptance.

3.content: The CLI and MoonBit SDK are not published yet. Start from the QuickGUI checkout ; its moon.work resolves the SDK locally: To scaffold a project, run bun packages/cli/src/cli.ts init ../my-app --frontend moonbit --no-install . Follow Project Structure to connect the generated module to this checkout.

4.content: Put this in main/main.mbt . Import egoist/quickgui/ui and egoist/quickgui/native in main/moon.pkg . Every component returns @ui.Element .

5.content: From the checkout, format and package the example: Development uses the fast native backend on Apple Silicon macOS and x64 Linux/Windows, reusing bridge and runtime objects in .quickgui/moonbit . Release builds and other hosts use the optimizing C backend. Set MOONBIT_NEW_NATIVE=0 to try the C backend during development.

6.content: For a larger application, run bun --cwd examples/quick-git-moonbit dev . Quick Git demonstrates multiple windows, menus, virtualized diffs, a history graph, and an independent I/O extension.

7.content: Configure MoonBit modules, the local SDK, and native packaging. A MoonBit app has a module, an executable package, and a QuickGUI configuration. Bun runs development tooling; the packaged app is a native executable.
7.keywords: moon.pkg moon.mod moon.work config toml workspace 项目 配置 設定

8.content: moon.mod declares the application module and SDK dependency. main/moon.pkg imports the packages used by the executable:

9.content: main/main.mbt defines main and the application’s components. Call @native.run once and create windows with @ui.window(component) . Each component returns an @ui.Element ; split larger applications into ordinary MoonBit packages.

10.content: frontend selects MoonBit; omitting it selects Go. entry names the executable package directory. Add extension directories containing quickgui.extension.json to native.extensions . quickgui build packages the executable, selected native libraries, fonts, and configured resources. .quickgui holds development output and caches; do not commit it.

11.content: Package Purpose egoist/quickgui/ui Components, styles, signals, memos, effects, cleanup, and routing. egoist/quickgui/native Windows, events, dialogs, menus, services, and extensions. egoist/quickgui/protocol Core property constants and mutation value types.

12.content: Until the SDK is published, create moon.work in a parent directory containing both your app and the QuickGUI checkout. Paths are relative to that workspace: From quickgui , run bun packages/cli/src/cli.ts dev --project ../my-app . This uses the local CLI without installing a published package.

13.content: Package the optional updater service for a MoonBit application.

14.content: Configure [updates] in quickgui.toml with your public key and download base URL. The TypeScript CLI creates appcast metadata and signed packages for both frontends.

15.content: MoonBit does not yet expose a dedicated updater-session helper. An application wrapper must manage the updater’s service ABI, session identity, check / install / automatic commands, and persistent extension-event subscriptions. The plain @native.invoke call does not return its request/session ID, so calling start alone is not a complete integration. See Authoring Extensions for the service contract.

16.content: Keep the updater session at application scope so closing one window does not stop updates. Handle completion errors and state events on the UI thread. Send the session’s stop request on cleanup; provider shutdown releases its remaining resources. An accepted installer handoff can outlive the session.

17.content: macOS uses Sparkle with signed app archives. The portable backend supports Windows installers and Linux AppImages. Build and validate on each target host; shipping a backend does not establish runtime acceptance for every platform.

18.content: Use quickgui keygen --sparkle to create signing keys and keep the private key outside the repository. Build with quickgui build , then publish the generated appcast and signed release archive at the configured download location.

19.content: Select the updater extension directory under [native].extensions . The CLI reads quickgui.extension.json inside it and packages the provider; MoonBit does not inspect Go imports. macOS uses Sparkle, and the other platforms use the compatible native updater service. Service wrappers use the same extension ABI described in Authoring Extensions .

20.content: Package independent native providers and call them from MoonBit. Extensions add optional native services without changing the core. Go and MoonBit share the same manifest and service ABI; each frontend supplies its own public wrapper.
20.keywords: extension authoring provider init-extension rust zig pure go manifest ABI 扩展 拡張

21.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Choose an extension type
21.content: The command accepts moonbit , rust , zig , or go . The MoonBit template builds a standalone service library with Bun, MoonBit (tested with v0.10.11), and a native C compiler. On Windows use an MSVC developer shell with cl or clang-cl and the Windows SDK. Set MOON , MOON_HOME , or CC to select tools. The provider itself needs neither Go nor the QuickGUI SDK; the included Go wrapper and demo show how another frontend can use it.

22.content: From the QuickGUI checkout, scaffold a provider:

23.content: Reusable MoonBit UI components are ordinary functions returning @ui.Element . Put them in a MoonBit package and accept content, callbacks, or getters as parameters. Pure UI components use the existing SDK and do not need a service provider or a new native library.

24.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Lay out a native extension
24.content: The scaffold separates native/ provider sources, artifacts/ libraries, and the optional Go wrapper and demo. The artifact directory carries quickgui.extension.json , target libraries, and package metadata. Keep application wrappers separate from provider implementation.

25.content: Directory paths are relative to the app project. The CLI reads quickgui.extension.json inside each directory; that manifest declares the provider name, version, and target artifacts. Build its library for each supported target. The CLI validates and packages explicitly selected providers and loads them before app startup. MoonBit does not discover extensions from Go imports.

26.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Declare dependencies › Invoke a service
26.content: For the generated my-service provider, a MoonBit wrapper can call: Call the wrapper inside a live component, event, or application owner. Replies use the registering owner’s lifetime. For ongoing sessions, subscribe to extension-event with window=0 , filter event.target to the session, and close the session on cleanup. Native worker threads must complete requests through the service ABI instead of calling MoonBit directly.

27.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Implement the native contract
27.content: Write service operations in native/extension.mbt : Inputs and successful replies are UTF-8 JSON bytes; errors are strings. Echoing the original bytes preserves nulls and large numbers. The adapter copies inputs into MoonBit-owned memory, checks the 64 KiB payload limit, emits the reply, and releases its native sink exactly once. Expected failures should return Err ; abort terminates the application. The generated adapter handles bounded synchronous operations on the application's UI worker. A nonblocking gate serializes runtime access, defers overlapping main-thread shutdown until the handler returns, and rejects concurrent or reentrant requests with a busy error. For slow native work or persistent sessions, extend the C adapter to copy input and retain the sink until completion. Workers must use the native reply/event callbacks and must not call MoonBit functions, retain the borrowed request context, or touch MoonBit-managed objects. Keep shutdown nonblocking. Implement the extension contract : versioned registration, method dispatch, asynchronous completion, and optional session events. No core integration is needed.

28.content: The CLI validates the explicitly selected manifests and loads each provider before application startup. The core checks its name, version, ABI, and service table, then routes operations by provider name. MoonBit does not discover providers through Go imports.

29.hierarchy: Authoring Extensions › Build and package artifacts
29.content: The build compiles MoonBit to C, then links a shared library with its own private runtime. Only the service descriptor is exported, so the provider can coexist with a MoonBit app and other providers. MoonBit's direct native backend does not yet produce shared-library packages ; this build path stays native and runs in the same process. Ordinary application edits reuse the built artifact. The manifest supplies the provider name, release version, and artifact package. Build through bun run build , and restart the demo after provider edits. --module sets the optional Go wrapper's module; edit native/moon.mod for the MoonBit provider module. moon -C native fmt formats the provider. The generated README covers the Go demo and local dependencies before publication.

30.content: Distribute a manifest, per-target native artifacts, and a MoonBit package exposing the service. The template stages the current host's library in artifacts/lib/<platform>-<arch>/ ; collect builds from each supported host and publish artifacts/ with its generated MoonBit license and notice. Consumers select the extension directory in quickgui.toml . For local development set QUICKGUI_EXTENSION_DIR to that absolute target directory. For direct executable runs, also declare @native.require_extension(name, version) before run and provide QUICKGUI_LIBRARY . Quick Git’s I/O extension demonstrates asynchronous process/file services. Its TypeScript launcher builds the provider once and reuses it during ordinary MoonBit edits.

31.content: Manage window lifetimes and asynchronous native work. Call @native.run once. Its startup callback creates windows and registers application services. Results and events run on the MoonBit UI thread.
31.keywords: window native lifecycle invoke watch_files with_owner 窗口 服务 ウィンドウ

32.content: Use @ui.window(component, options=...) to create a window; each window owns an independent tree. @native.current_window() is valid while building a component or handling a window callback. Capture that handle for later .close() or .focus() calls. Creation is asynchronous. Wait for window-ready-to-show before querying native geometry or state. Set show: false to prepare a hidden window. Options use the native JSON schema, including title , width , height , background , titleBarStyle , trafficLightX , and trafficLightY .

33.hierarchy: Windows & Native Services › Commands and services
33.content: @native.command(json, callback) sends platform commands. @native.invoke(operation, params, callback) calls an asynchronous native service. Both callbacks receive Result[Json, String] . Use them for operations that need a response. @native.call is restricted to the core’s synchronous CPU-only allowlist. Callbacks belong to their registering owner. If an operation should survive the row or dialog that starts it, register it inside window.with_owner(() => { ... }) . Closing that window still retires the callback.

34.hierarchy: Windows & Native Services › Events and file watching
34.content: @native.on_event(kind, listener) subscribes in the current window context. @native.subscribe also returns a cancellation function. Use window=0 for application-level events. @native.watch_files(paths, changed, ready) uses OS file notifications and returns a stop function. These subscriptions are cleaned up with their owner. Persistent extension events use extension-event ; filter event.target to the session you opened. See Authoring Extensions .

35.content: Signals connect state to the text and properties that read it. Updates change retained nodes without rerunning the entire component.
35.keywords: signal reactivity memo effect batch cleanup

36.content: @ui.create_signal(initial) returns (read, write) . A call such as @ui.text("Count: \{count()}") is reactive when built with QuickGUI. The compiler also tracks expressions in button content, native properties, fluent styles, interaction styles, and child lists. Each binding updates its own retained nodes; the component does not rerun. Binding expressions must be pure. Ordinary setup remains ordinary MoonBit: let initial = count() captures a snapshot. Event handlers run only on events. Use @ui.untrack(count) for an untracked read. Custom components returning @ui.Element use plain parameter types: label(count()) preserves a live input, and reads of that parameter in the child’s view subscribe to it. A setup copy such as let initial = count inside the child remains a snapshot. Explicit getter parameters still work. Explicit bind_* methods and the lower-level Signal handle remain available for manual composition and keyed rows.

37.content: @ui.create_memo caches a value calculated from signals and updates its dependents when the result changes. It returns a read-only getter, called as total() . Keep the calculation pure: use a memo for derived values and an effect for external work. The total below recalculates when quantity changes.

38.content: @ui.create_effect runs initially and again when a signal it read changes. Reads in conditional branches become dependencies only when that branch executes. Use effects for external work, such as synchronizing a subscription; view expressions already bind text and properties. This example logs subscription startup and teardown. Cleanup registered inside the effect runs before its next execution and when its owner is disposed. Capturing current ensures that teardown uses the old topic. Cleanup registered outside an effect belongs to the surrounding owner and runs when it is disposed, rather than on each signal update. Removing a dynamic branch or closing a window disposes its owned effects and callbacks.

39.content: @ui.batch groups synchronous writes so dependent effects flush after the outermost batch. Both fields below change together: the effect logs “Grace Hopper” without logging an intermediate “Grace Lovelace”. Native event handlers already batch writes, and the explicit batch preserves that behavior when apply_profile is called from other UI code. Signal reads and writes belong on the UI thread. A batch does not make background access thread-safe. Use @ui.untrack(read) when an effect needs a snapshot that should not become a dependency. Avoid using an effect to copy one signal into another when a memo can express the derived value.

40.content: Components construct a retained tree once when mounted. Reactive bindings update the affected nodes; the native core handles layout, painting, and accessibility.
40.keywords: rendering retained children mount lifecycle keyed

41.content: Constructors accept only children or content. Empty containers use [] ; buttons also accept a string or one element. Apply styles, properties, and event handlers through fluent methods such as .padding(24) , .checked(checked()) , and .on_click(save) . Use .style(shared) for reusable styles. Read getters directly in fluent properties: @ui.checkbox([]).checked(checked()).on_checked_change(set_checked) . Literal properties initialize component-owned state; expressions containing signal reads become controlled bindings. Styles merge in declaration order. Use child lists throughout; scoped parts can attach a complete list with .children([...]) .

42.content: The branch factory runs when the predicate switches branches. Put values that change within that branch in bindings so its nodes can stay mounted.

43.content: Keys must be unique and stable. The render callback receives a row signal, so existing rows can update without replacing native node IDs or local state. Keyed children alone do not virtualize a long list; use table visible ranges .

44.content: @ui.window(component, options=...) gives each window its own retained tree and owner. Closing it disposes its nodes, bindings, and callbacks. Use @ui.on_cleanup for component resources; do not move retained nodes between windows.

45.content: Capture @native.current_window() while constructing a component or handling its events. Keep the handle for later .close() or .focus() calls. Register longer-lived work through window.with_owner(...) . See Windows & Native Services for asynchronous creation and service ownership.

46.content: Use quickgui check and quickgui test so tests receive the same view transform as builds. Add --release for release-backend tests. Raw moon check checks the original types, while raw moon test bypasses implicit view bindings. The CLI preserves source files and maps compiler diagnostics, assertion failures, and symbolicated stack locations back to them. Native debugger breakpoints and stepping currently use the generated files in .quickgui/moonbit-sources ; original-file breakpoint mapping is not supported yet. Editor completion and type checking continue to use ordinary MoonBit.

47.content: Use MoonBit primitives, native table parts, and resizable panels. MoonBit provides the same native component families as Go, using child lists and fluent styles, properties, and event handlers. The sidebar includes the full component reference and macOS SwiftUI hosts.
47.keywords: components table virtualization visibleRange splitter resizable_panel svg markdown 表格 组件 テーブル

48.content: A MoonBit component is a function returning @ui.Element . Compose it in a child list. Use plain typed parameters and pass signal reads directly. The QuickGUI compiler preserves live expressions through component calls, including imported workspace components. Components construct once and their native bindings track the props they read; no annotation or special prop type is needed. Reusable containers can accept an array of children and spread them after their own heading. The nested native expressions still create independent bindings. The title parameter accepts either a static string or a live expression such as title() . Creating a local copy inside the component intentionally captures a setup snapshot.

49.content: Constructor Content view([...]) Container accepting only a child list. Apply styles and handlers with fluent methods. text(value) Static or reactive text. button(content) A button with native input behavior. input() Text input with value and event bindings. image(source) / svg(source) Images or tinted SVG masks. markdown(source) Native Markdown content.

50.content: Create a root such as checkbox([]) , tabs([]) or dialog([]) , then create related parts with root.slot(@ui.Indicator) or root.slot(@ui.Panel, value="settings") . Parts share the root scope automatically. Descendants of an accordion item also inherit its value and index. Set initial state with .checked(false) or .active_value("overview") ; use .bind_checked(...) or .bind_active_value(...) and a change callback for controlled state. Every builder returns an Element . The raw .part(...) API remains available for extensions.

51.content: Read signal getters in .checked(checked()) or .active_value(value()) , and write changes through the corresponding callbacks. Literals initialize component-owned state. Explicit bind_* methods remain available when composing bindings manually. Every native control has a dedicated page in the Components sidebar. For complete workflows, see Forms & Input and Overlays & Dialogs .

53.content: The MoonBit components example includes all 43 demos from the Go gallery, with the same sidebar and light/dark appearance. Explore mixed and read-only controls, animated switches, pickers, native menus, dialogs, a virtual table with 5,000 rows, and lazy tree children. From a source checkout with MoonBit and the native host library installed: Run bun --cwd examples/components-moonbit check for the SDK and gallery tests, or add --native to present every demo in both appearances through the native host.

54.hierarchy: Components › Component families › Tables and visible rows
54.content: table([]).columns(columns).row_count(rows).row_height(height) binds column definitions and the full row count. Add table_row([]).row_index(index) and table_cell([]).column(column_id) parts. The core handles layout, scrolling, keyboard selection, and accessibility. This small table mounts all three rows: For large data, listen to .on_change(...) and retain its visibleRange field when present. Pass that field to @ui.visible_range(range, count) and mount only [start, end) with children_keyed . The end is exclusive; the initial range is bounded to 40 rows. Selection events may omit visibleRange , so do not reset the range on every event. selectedRanges reports selection with inclusive range ends. Bind controlled selection through @protocol.SELECTION . See Quick Git’s table usage for virtualized history and diff rows.

55.content: The core tracks the drag and updates pane geometry. The callback reports the width for application state or persistence; it is not part of pointer tracking.

56.content: Every compound part is an Element , so it accepts the same .style(shared) , layout, typography, and interaction modifiers as a primitive. Create parts with .slot(...) to retain their root scope and item identity. Reuse builders as described in Styling & Layout .

57.content: The router selects components from the current application path and keeps a navigation history. Routes render native QuickGUI content in the current window.
57.keywords: router route layout outlet navigation history parameters

58.content: Build a route tree with @ui.router([...]) and @ui.route(path, render) . Each render callback receives the router and returns an element. Mount router.outlet() where the active route belongs; initial="/settings" selects a starting destination.

59.content: Declare routes with @ui.route . Use @ui.layout to share surrounding content, and call its outlet() callback where the matched child belongs. Mount the router with router.outlet() . Outlets retain nodes by matched route identity. Navigating between sibling routes keeps their common layout and its state. Read router.state() in a binding for the current location and matched parameters; router.is_active(path) tests a navigation destination.

60.content: Use router.link(path, label) for a navigation link. router.navigate(path) pushes history; pass replace=true to replace the current entry. router.go(-1) goes back and router.go(1) goes forward. A shared navigation component can receive the router from its layout callback. The active-link weight below tracks route changes, while Back and Forward move through this router’s in-memory history. These controls navigate within the current window.

61.content: Dynamic route patterns such as /projects/:id share the native router’s matching rules. Read router.state() in a binding to inspect the current location and matched.params JSON. router.is_active(path) tests a navigation destination. Keep the router in the component that owns its history.

62.content: Compose fluent styles, merge declarations, and bind native state styles. Element methods and @ui.style() share the same native style properties. Numeric dimensions are pixels; strings support percentages and native keywords.
62.keywords: style fluent merge flexbox color hover layout 样式 布局 スタイル

63.content: Use .flex_row() , .flex_col() , .items_center() , and .justify_center() for common layouts. .flex_1() sets grow, shrink, and a zero basis. Give scrollable flex children .min_height(0) and a bounded parent size.

64.content: .style(base).style(overrides) merges declarations in order; later properties win. .merge(other) does the same for style builders. Applying a style takes a snapshot. Changing the builder later does not update the mounted element. The compiler binds getter reads inside .style(...) and fluent modifiers. Later declarations keep precedence on every update; disappearing declarations are cleared or reveal an earlier fallback. Interaction-style callbacks can also read getters. Mutating an already-applied reusable builder is still a snapshot mutation, so derive styles from signals instead.

65.content: @ui.style() returns a reusable @ui.Style . Apply it to elements or compound parts with .style(shared) . Builders are mutable: derive a separate style with @ui.style().merge(base) before adding overrides. Applying a style snapshots its declarations; later builder changes do not update mounted nodes.

66.content: Use .flex() , .flex_row() , or .flex_col() for flex layouts. .flex_1() sets grow 1, shrink 1, and zero basis. Scrolling children need .min_height(0) or .min_width(0) and a bounded parent. The same methods work on @ui.style() .

67.content: Use .grid_cols(3) for equal columns or .grid_template_columns("220px 1fr") for explicit tracks. .col_span_full() , .col_start(...) , and .col_span(...) place children. Elements and styles share Rust’s layout helpers and four-pixel spacing scale.

68.content: Use @ui.rgb8(r, g, b) or @ui.rgba8(r, g, b, a) , with channels from 0 to 255. Window options accept these colors as JSON values; a raw integer uses 0xAABBGGRR ( 0 for transparent). Do not pass CSS color strings as a window’s background . @ui.svg(source) produces a mask tinted by .text_color(...) . For multiple graph colors, use separate tinted SVG layers, as shown in Quick Git.

69.content: Use .hover(s => ...) , .active(s => ...) , and .focus_style(s => ...) for native pointer and focus states. .selected_style styles selected compound parts. These states are resolved by the native core. For a drop target’s drag-over appearance, use bind_json with @protocol.DRAG_OVER_STYLE and return a style’s .json() . Configure the node as a drop target as well; a style does not enable drop behavior. Import egoist/quickgui/protocol when using protocol constants. Add transitions to the base style to animate state changes. Declare the resting appearance on the element and only the changed paint properties in each state. Hover temporarily overrides the background; pressing lowers opacity. Neither state needs a signal or a component rerender.

70.hierarchy: Styling & Layout › Groups and named group hover
70.content: .group("card") names an ancestor group. MoonBit exposes group paint rules through .bind_json(@protocol.GROUP_HOVER_STYLE, read) and GROUP_ACTIVE_STYLE . Supply the core’s rule array with a group name and paint fields; a style builder’s .json() produces the paint declaration. Import egoist/quickgui/protocol for these constants. Named rules follow the nearest ancestor with the matching name; unnamed rules follow the nearest group. Repeated rules apply in order, and the node’s own hover style wins for overlapping properties. FOCUS_WITHIN_STYLE follows focus in the node or descendants. These states do not change layout and cannot set the cursor.

71.content: Animate retained paint properties without per-frame MoonBit work. Transitions interpolate native style changes on an existing element. Declare a target and timing; the core advances the frames and stops requesting them when complete.
71.keywords: transition animation easing duration transform reduced motion 动画 过渡 アニメーション

72.content: Put timing on the base element so both entering and leaving a state animate. A signal-driven bind_style target uses the same transition. Changing a target mid-transition starts from the current visible value.

73.content: Read a signal in a fluent target style. The view compiler binds that target on the retained element, and the native core interpolates its changes. Keep the same node mounted while the value changes.

74.hierarchy: Transitions & Animation › Timing and frame rate
74.content: Durations are milliseconds, bounded to 0–10 seconds. .transition_easing(...) accepts linear , ease , ease-in , ease-out , or ease-in-out . .transition_max_fps(30) optionally caps the frame rate; omit it to follow presentation. One element has one duration, easing, and frame-rate cap for its selected properties. Delays and custom cubic Bézier curves are not supported.

75.content: Transition background-color , border-color , border-width , border-radius , color , opacity , box-shadow , and transform . all selects these paint properties. Width, height, padding, gradients, and other layout changes do not interpolate. Use a transform for a sliding thumb instead of animating its layout position.

76.hierarchy: Transitions & Animation › Mounting and reduced motion
76.content: Initial styles apply directly. Keep an element mounted to animate a target change; child_if removes a branch immediately and does not wait for an exit fade. Zero opacity still occupies layout and accepts input. Transitions respect the system Reduce Motion preference. Hidden or occluded windows pause local transitions.

77.content: For an animated image, use @ui.image(path) with a GIF or WebP. The native decoder retains frames and repeat policy; no signal timer is needed.

78.content: Bind text fields, submit handlers, and disabled controls to signals. Keep editable values in signals and write user changes back through event handlers. The native input keeps selection, focus, and text editing behavior.
78.keywords: input form submit bind_value disabled readonly 输入 表单 フォーム

79.content: on_input receives the updated string. on_submit receives the submitted string. Use .focus() on a retained input handle when moving focus programmatically.

80.hierarchy: Forms & Input › Text input › Disabled and read-only
80.content: .bind_disabled(() => disabled.get()) changes actual native interaction state. A dimmed style alone does not disable a control. Use .property(@protocol.READ_ONLY, @protocol.Boolean(true)) for read-only input, and .property(@protocol.PLACEHOLDER, @protocol.Text("Name")) for a placeholder. Import egoist/quickgui/protocol for these constants. Use bind_style or native state styles for appearance, and the corresponding property for behavior.

81.content: Use @ui.field([]) and its Label, Control, Description, and Error slots to connect a field’s label and validation content. The native core owns their semantic relationships. See Field for validation and form integration.

82.content: Use Checkbox , Switch , Select and the other control pages in the sidebar. Their helpers wire native roles, values and scope. Read-only and disabled controls suppress default changes; Event.prevent_default() can cancel an application event without removing component behavior.

83.content: @ui.select([]).items(items).active_value(value()) builds a picker from the native item model. Wire its change callback back to your selection signal. Use the Select reference for single and multiple selection and popup parts.

84.content: .on_input(handler) and .on_submit(handler) receive strings. Semantic controls report changes through their component callbacks. Use event-aware handlers when propagation or Event.prevent_default() matters. Set .disabled(...) and .read_only(...) for behavior; styling alone does not disable editing.

85.content: Open system dialogs and native menus from MoonBit components. Capture the current window while constructing a component. Its methods present OS dialogs and popup menus, with results delivered asynchronously.
85.keywords: menu dialog file picker popup_menu context menu 菜单 对话框 メニュー ダイアログ

86.content: Create a trigger, positioner, and popup from @ui.popover([]) . The native core handles placement, collisions, focus, and dismissal.

87.content: Create modal content from @ui.dialog([]) and its Portal, Backdrop, Popup, Title, Description, and Close slots. The core keeps focus inside the modal and owns dismissal.

88.content: @ui.system_popover([]).system_content(...) creates content in a separate native child window. Provide its size and placement, and create its QuickGUI nodes inside the content callback.

90.hierarchy: Overlays & Dialogs › Native dialogs › Choose a directory
90.content: Dialog kind 0 is an alert, 1 opens paths, and 2 saves a path. Open/save results contain a paths array; an empty selection is cancellation. Alerts return the chosen button identifier. Handle the Result instead of blocking the UI thread.

91.hierarchy: Overlays & Dialogs › Native dialogs › Popup and context menus
91.content: popup_menu keeps action callbacks alive until the menu dismisses. Use submenu for nested items and menu_role for standard platform commands. Event handlers and menu items retain the registering owner.

92.hierarchy: Overlays & Dialogs › Native dialogs › Application menus and overlays
92.content: Call @native.set_application_menu(items) inside the application startup callback to install app-level menus. Use platform roles for commands such as closing, hiding, or minimizing a window. Use Dialog , Popover , SystemPopover and Tooltip for their native focus, dismissal and lifetime behavior. Components retain their parts and let the core handle transition completion. Model-driven popover_menu([]) uses .when_open(...) to mount its popup only while open.

93.content: Host native macOS controls from MoonBit.

94.content: Create SwiftUI controls under @ui.swift_ui_host([]) . They require macOS. The sidebar lists every supported SwiftUI control.

95.content: The SwiftUI family includes buttons, sliders, toggles, progress views, steppers, text and secure fields, pickers, date and color pickers, and gauges. Open each control’s sidebar reference for its properties and events.

.group("card") names an ancestor group. MoonBit exposes group paint rules through .bind_json(@protocol.GROUP_HOVER_STYLE, read) and GROUP_ACTIVE_STYLE . Supply the core’s rule array with a group name and paint fields; a style builder’s .json() produces the paint declaration. Import egoist/quickgui/protocol for these constants. Named rules follow the nearest ancestor with the matching name; unnamed rules follow the nearest group. Repeated rules apply in order, and the node’s own hover style wins for overlapping properties. FOCUS_WITHIN_STYLE follows focus in the node or descendants. These states do not change layout and cannot set the cursor.

.on_input(handler) and .on_submit(handler) receive strings. Semantic controls report changes through their component callbacks. Use event-aware handlers when propagation or Event.prevent_default() matters. Set .disabled(...) and .read_only(...) for behavior; styling alone does not disable editing.

.style(base).style(overrides) merges declarations in order; later properties win. .merge(other) does the same for style builders. Applying a style takes a snapshot. Changing the builder later does not update the mounted element. The compiler binds getter reads inside .style(...) and fluent modifiers. Later declarations keep precedence on every update; disappearing declarations are cleared or reveal an earlier fallback. Interaction-style callbacks can also read getters. Mutating an already-applied reusable builder is still a snapshot mutation, so derive styles from signals instead.

@native.command(json, callback) sends platform commands. @native.invoke(operation, params, callback) calls an asynchronous native service. Both callbacks receive Result[Json, String] . Use them for operations that need a response. @native.call is restricted to the core’s synchronous CPU-only allowlist. Callbacks belong to their registering owner. If an operation should survive the row or dialog that starts it, register it inside window.with_owner(() => { ... }) . Closing that window still retires the callback.

@native.on_event(kind, listener) subscribes in the current window context. @native.subscribe also returns a cancellation function. Use window=0 for application-level events. @native.watch_files(paths, changed, ready) uses OS file notifications and returns a stop function. These subscriptions are cleaned up with their owner. Persistent extension events use extension-event ; filter event.target to the session you opened. See Authoring Extensions .

@ui.batch groups synchronous writes so dependent effects flush after the outermost batch. Both fields below change together: the effect logs “Grace Hopper” without logging an intermediate “Grace Lovelace”. Native event handlers already batch writes, and the explicit batch preserves that behavior when apply_profile is called from other UI code. Signal reads and writes belong on the UI thread. A batch does not make background access thread-safe. Use @ui.untrack(read) when an effect needs a snapshot that should not become a dependency. Avoid using an effect to copy one signal into another when a memo can express the derived value.

@ui.create_effect runs initially and again when a signal it read changes. Reads in conditional branches become dependencies only when that branch executes. Use effects for external work, such as synchronizing a subscription; view expressions already bind text and properties. This example logs subscription startup and teardown. Cleanup registered inside the effect runs before its next execution and when its owner is disposed. Capturing current ensures that teardown uses the old topic. Cleanup registered outside an effect belongs to the surrounding owner and runs when it is disposed, rather than on each signal update. Removing a dynamic branch or closing a window disposes its owned effects and callbacks.

@ui.create_memo caches a value calculated from signals and updates its dependents when the result changes. It returns a read-only getter, called as total() . Keep the calculation pure: use a memo for derived values and an effect for external work. The total below recalculates when quantity changes.

@ui.create_signal(initial) returns (read, write) . A call such as @ui.text("Count: \{count()}") is reactive when built with QuickGUI. The compiler also tracks expressions in button content, native properties, fluent styles, interaction styles, and child lists. Each binding updates its own retained nodes; the component does not rerun. Binding expressions must be pure. Ordinary setup remains ordinary MoonBit: let initial = count() captures a snapshot. Event handlers run only on events. Use @ui.untrack(count) for an untracked read. Custom components returning @ui.Element use plain parameter types: label(count()) preserves a live input, and reads of that parameter in the child’s view subscribe to it. A setup copy such as let initial = count inside the child remains a snapshot. Explicit getter parameters still work. Explicit bind_* methods and the lower-level Signal handle remain available for manual composition and keyed rows.

@ui.select([]).items(items).active_value(value()) builds a picker from the native item model. Wire its change callback back to your selection signal. Use the Select reference for single and multiple selection and popup parts.

@ui.style() returns a reusable @ui.Style . Apply it to elements or compound parts with .style(shared) . Builders are mutable: derive a separate style with @ui.style().merge(base) before adding overrides. Applying a style snapshots its declarations; later builder changes do not update mounted nodes.
@ui.system_popover([]).system_content(...) creates content in a separate native child window. Provide its size and placement, and create its QuickGUI nodes inside the content callback.

@ui.window(component, options=...) gives each window its own retained tree and owner. Closing it disposes its nodes, bindings, and callbacks. Use @ui.on_cleanup for component resources; do not move retained nodes between windows.

Distribute a manifest, per-target native artifacts, and a MoonBit package exposing the service. The template stages the current host's library in artifacts/lib/<platform>-<arch>/ ; collect builds from each supported host and publish artifacts/ with its generated MoonBit license and notice. Consumers select the extension directory in quickgui.toml . For local development set QUICKGUI_EXTENSION_DIR to that absolute target directory. For direct executable runs, also declare @native.require_extension(name, version) before run and provide QUICKGUI_LIBRARY . Quick Git’s I/O extension demonstrates asynchronous process/file services. Its TypeScript launcher builds the provider once and reuses it during ordinary MoonBit edits.

Durations are milliseconds, bounded to 0–10 seconds. .transition_easing(...) accepts linear , ease , ease-in , ease-out , or ease-in-out . .transition_max_fps(30) optionally caps the frame rate; omit it to follow presentation. One element has one duration, easing, and frame-rate cap for its selected properties. Delays and custom cubic Bézier curves are not supported.

The build compiles MoonBit to C, then links a shared library with its own private runtime. Only the service descriptor is exported, so the provider can coexist with a MoonBit app and other providers. MoonBit's direct native backend does not yet produce shared-library packages ; this build path stays native and runs in the same process. Ordinary application edits reuse the built artifact. The manifest supplies the provider name, release version, and artifact package. Build through bun run build , and restart the demo after provider edits. --module sets the optional Go wrapper's module; edit native/moon.mod for the MoonBit provider module. moon -C native fmt formats the provider. The generated README covers the Go demo and local dependencies before publication.

The CLI and MoonBit SDK are not published yet. Start from the QuickGUI checkout ; its moon.work resolves the SDK locally: To scaffold a project, run bun packages/cli/src/cli.ts init ../my-app --frontend moonbit --no-install . Follow Project Structure to connect the generated module to this checkout.

The CLI validates the explicitly selected manifests and loads each provider before application startup. The core checks its name, version, ABI, and service table, then routes operations by provider name. MoonBit does not discover providers through Go imports.

The command accepts moonbit , rust , zig , or go . The MoonBit template builds a standalone service library with Bun, MoonBit (tested with v0.10.11), and a native C compiler. On Windows use an MSVC developer shell with cl or clang-cl and the Windows SDK. Set MOON , MOON_HOME , or CC to select tools. The provider itself needs neither Go nor the QuickGUI SDK; the included Go wrapper and demo show how another frontend can use it.

Until the SDK is published, create moon.work in a parent directory containing both your app and the QuickGUI checkout. Paths are relative to that workspace: From quickgui , run bun packages/cli/src/cli.ts dev --project ../my-app . This uses the local CLI without installing a published package.

Use .flex_row() , .flex_col() , .items_center() , and .justify_center() for common layouts. .flex_1() sets grow, shrink, and a zero basis. Give scrollable flex children .min_height(0) and a bounded parent size.

Use .flex() , .flex_row() , or .flex_col() for flex layouts. .flex_1() sets grow 1, shrink 1, and zero basis. Scrolling children need .min_height(0) or .min_width(0) and a bounded parent. The same methods work on @ui.style() .

Use .grid_cols(3) for equal columns or .grid_template_columns("220px 1fr") for explicit tracks. .col_span_full() , .col_start(...) , and .col_span(...) place children. Elements and styles share Rust’s layout helpers and four-pixel spacing scale.

Use .hover(s => ...) , .active(s => ...) , and .focus_style(s => ...) for native pointer and focus states. .selected_style styles selected compound parts. These states are resolved by the native core. For a drop target’s drag-over appearance, use bind_json with @protocol.DRAG_OVER_STYLE and return a style’s .json() . Configure the node as a drop target as well; a style does not enable drop behavior. Import egoist/quickgui/protocol when using protocol constants. Add transitions to the base style to animate state changes. Declare the resting appearance on the element and only the changed paint properties in each state. Hover temporarily overrides the background; pressing lowers opacity. Neither state needs a signal or a component rerender.

Use @ui.field([]) and its Label, Control, Description, and Error slots to connect a field’s label and validation content. The native core owns their semantic relationships. See Field for validation and form integration.

Use @ui.rgb8(r, g, b) or @ui.rgba8(r, g, b, a) , with channels from 0 to 255. Window options accept these colors as JSON values; a raw integer uses 0xAABBGGRR ( 0 for transparent). Do not pass CSS color strings as a window’s background . @ui.svg(source) produces a mask tinted by .text_color(...) . For multiple graph colors, use separate tinted SVG layers, as shown in Quick Git.

Use @ui.window(component, options=...) to create a window; each window owns an independent tree. @native.current_window() is valid while building a component or handling a window callback. Capture that handle for later .close() or .focus() calls. Creation is asynchronous. Wait for window-ready-to-show before querying native geometry or state. Set show: false to prepare a hidden window. Options use the native JSON schema, including title , width , height , background , titleBarStyle , trafficLightX , and trafficLightY .

Use Checkbox , Switch , Select and the other control pages in the sidebar. Their helpers wire native roles, values and scope. Read-only and disabled controls suppress default changes; Event.prevent_default() can cancel an application event without removing component behavior.

Use MoonBit primitives, native table parts, and resizable panels. MoonBit provides the same native component families as Go, using child lists and fluent styles, properties, and event handlers. The sidebar includes the full component reference and macOS SwiftUI hosts.

Use quickgui check and quickgui test so tests receive the same view transform as builds. Add --release for release-backend tests. Raw moon check checks the original types, while raw moon test bypasses implicit view bindings. The CLI preserves source files and maps compiler diagnostics, assertion failures, and symbolicated stack locations back to them. Native debugger breakpoints and stepping currently use the generated files in .quickgui/moonbit-sources ; original-file breakpoint mapping is not supported yet. Editor completion and type checking continue to use ordinary MoonBit.

Use quickgui keygen --sparkle to create signing keys and keep the private key outside the repository. Build with quickgui build , then publish the generated appcast and signed release archive at the configured download location.

Use router.link(path, label) for a navigation link. router.navigate(path) pushes history; pass replace=true to replace the current entry. router.go(-1) goes back and router.go(1) goes forward. A shared navigation component can receive the router from its layout callback. The active-link weight below tracks route changes, while Back and Forward move through this router’s in-memory history. Write service operations in native/extension.mbt : Inputs and successful replies are UTF-8 JSON bytes; errors are strings. Echoing the original bytes preserves nulls and large numbers. The adapter copies inputs into MoonBit-owned memory, checks the 64 KiB payload limit, emits the reply, and releases its native sink exactly once. Expected failures should return Err ; abort terminates the application. The generated adapter handles bounded synchronous operations on the application's UI worker. A nonblocking gate serializes runtime access, defers overlapping main-thread shutdown until the handler returns, and rejects concurrent or reentrant requests with a busy error. For slow native work or persistent sessions, extend the C adapter to copy input and retain the sink until completion. Workers must use the native reply/event callbacks and must not call MoonBit functions, retain the borrowed request context, or touch MoonBit-managed objects. Keep shutdown nonblocking. Implement the extension contract : versioned registration, method dispatch, asynchronous completion, and optional session events. No core integration is needed.
